blocks.text: Saishreek Singh | Solo student entry | 23 November 2026

We test whether sparse spectral descriptors add unseen-site predictive value to an official satellite/table baseline for five standardized atmospheric and thermal targets. Using 3,218 observations from 81 sites, we compare fixed regularized regressors and inner-site-selected convex mixtures. On the same 64 development sites, adding a FIRMS-only spectral branch reduces masked mean column-wise RMSE from 0.93378 to 0.91950, wins two of three outer folds and improves pooled environmental-holdout error from 0.96628 to 0.94620. Four non-FIRMS predictions are unchanged. Quality-only and brightness-only controls are weaker; a shuffled control is nearly as strong, limiting spatial attribution. A fresh-process reproduction and strict export identity checks protect the released fallback. These reused-development results do not establish calibrated fire detection, physical emissions or private/future-time accuracy.

Can relative B8A/B11/B12 spectral shape and local context recover signal diluted by global chip summaries? Our contribution is an independently implemented, literature-informed feature experiment with explicit controls and reproducible acceptance gates. We distinguish measured predictive utility from an explanation of its physical mechanism. Sparse local structure is a hypothesis, not a proven novel fire retrieval. Earlier flood/NDVI/terrain studies inform LavaLabs interface conventions, but are not atmospheric validation or additional competition observations.

Predict the five released targets, then prioritize verification: inspect transfer error, high-error sites and missing-observation support before deploying an indicator. Anonymous standardized targets do not support named-facility enforcement, rescue routing, physical pollution thresholds or a dated future forecast.

Only organizer-supplied inputs are used: 29 numerical predictors, 3,218 training rows, 1,221 test rows and 4,439 fourteen-layer Sentinel-2 chips. The twelve optical layers are Level-2A surface reflectance scaled by 10,000; SCL and cloud probability are supplied separately. B8A, B11 and B12 are zero-based layers 8, 10 and 11. True locations, dates and physical pixel size are unavailable. Sample IDs only join/export; site keys only partition. No external observations or location/date reconstruction are used.

Targets refer to fixed 10 km windows, while chip framing varies. Gas labels are coarse site-window values relative to a surrounding background; all five targets use training-set standardization. FIRMS is a detection-derived thermal indicator, not an annotated fire mask. Its no-detection floor is a real label, not missingness. Absence of a chip hotspot cannot force a floor prediction. Missing target labels are excluded per target, never replaced by zero.

The frozen control combines the 29 table fields with the official 54 image summaries. Spectral arithmetic converts unsigned integers to float first and retains reflectances above one. An observability mask excludes SCL 0/1; clear background also excludes SCL 3/8/9/10 and cloud probability at least 40%. We compute positive (B12-B11)/max(B8A,0.02), subtract its valid-weighted 15 by 15 local mean and retain at most 32 positive local-excess pixels with positive B12-2B11+B8A. Numerical epsilon is 1e-10; ties use pixel position.

Six descriptors summarize excess, candidate count and eight-connected component structure. Six more summarize relative B8A/B11/B12 excess against a local median background, NIR/SWIR relationships, nonclear candidates and background support. Background requires at least 16 clear pixels and excludes the central 3 by 3 patch and selected candidates. Four global quality summaries yield a 99-feature full branch. No-data summaries remain unavailable. Constants are fixed engineering choices, not calibrated physical fire thresholds. The 32-chip label-blind pilot passed and six private overlays were reviewed; candidates on reflective/water edges expose false-fire interpretations. No thresholds were retuned.

GroupShuffleSplit with seed 2026 retains the historical 64-site, 2,597-row development subset. Three shuffled outer GroupKFold partitions use seed 2026; three inner whole-site folds select mixtures. HistGradientBoosting settings remain fixed: 250 iterations, learning rate 0.04, depth 3, minimum leaf 40, L2 5, feature fraction 0.6, seed 0, no early stopping. Only observed fitting labels train each model; fit-only all-missing feature columns are omitted. Four targets retain exact control predictions. FIRMS selects one of 45 fixed convex combinations of table, official-image and new-branch predictions plus the fitting mean, using inner labels only.

The sole candidate is the full twelve-descriptor branch. Predeclared alternatives diagnose quality, B12 brightness, the first six descriptors, and a fixed joint pixel permutation that preserves spectra but breaks neighborhoods. Promotion requires pooled gain at least 0.005, at least two fold wins, no target regression above 0.02, improvement over quality/brightness controls, no pooled environmental-stress regression and a positive conditional bootstrap lower bound. Two feature-only KMeans environmental clusters use site-median weather/terrain, with 36 and 28 sites; each is held out in turn. Neither targets nor test rows determine this partition.

Full spectral improves MCRMSE by 0.0142833 and FIRMS RMSE by 0.0714163, with two of three outer-fold wins. The first four target predictions and label denominators match exactly. A separate implementation rereads saved OOF arrays, verifies truth/site identity and recomputes every target RMSE and denominator. The 1,000-draw paired-site bootstrap gain interval is [0.00228788, 0.02501520]; it conditions on fixed OOF predictions and excludes retraining/model-selection uncertainty.

The shuffled branch is only 0.0003556 MCRMSE worse than the full branch. Consequently these results do not isolate neighborhood structure as the source of improvement. Earlier global cloud/spatial variants failed their development comparison; separate Mitra, TabPFN and deeper-tree trials failed their fixed promotion gates. Their negative results remain archived. The full spectral branch alone is eligible; diagnostic alternatives are not retrospectively selected for export.

The spectral follow-up does not rescore the older 17-site acceptance partition. Earlier official-image confirmation was 0.86206 versus table 0.88725, but that partition influenced acceptance and was never untouched final-test evidence. Public and private sites/periods differ from training. Public scoring uses a minority of test rows; development gains must not be presented as leaderboard gains. The first raw-table submission scored 1.32129. Fixed CatBoost improved reused-development error to 0.93120 but scored 1.16407 publicly, demonstrating a local/public reversal.

The private interactive experiment extracted all 4,439 chips in 572.7 seconds; extraction plus grouped comparisons took 690.53 seconds. The accepted all-training refit took 28.36 seconds. CPU numerical work uses two threads; no GPU, new package or pretrained weights are required. Final FIRMS weights come from five whole-site OOF folds on all permitted training data, followed by a full fit. The complete original control CSV hash is reproduced before changing only FIRMS. The candidate contains 1,221 ordered string IDs and five finite predictions. A fresh saved Save and Run All version must reproduce grouped metrics and the candidate hash before scoring.

Fresh saved private version 373122625 completed successfully in 767.2 seconds and reproduced the development/stress results and candidate CSV hash exactly. The single genuine submission completed with public MCRMSE 1.13057, versus 1.15808 for the old HistGB finalist (2.38% lower public error). Both are selected; CatBoost is no longer selected. No post-score mixture or parameter change was made. Private accuracy is unknown.

Eleven new feature/controller/refit checks pass locally and in private Kaggle, covering arithmetic, band identity, missingness, off-center patches, cache identity/corruption, outer-label independence, site boundaries and failed-gate/export-identity refusal. These are software checks, not detection-accuracy validation. Five sites account for 52.5% of control FIRMS squared error. The 260 examples above the development 90th percentile improve from 2.63674 to 2.47266 FIRMS RMSE; the other 2,337 improve from 0.71317 to 0.66111. These descriptive strata have different denominators and are not independent performance tests.

All development is reused and subject to selection optimism. Only 81 sites and sparse CH4 support are available. No calibrated uncertainty, physical FRP/temperature/flux, field verification or forward-time accuracy is established. The fixed-OOF bootstrap does not resolve these limitations. Restricted rows, identifiers, chips, feature matrices and predictions remain private on Kaggle; only source and permitted aggregate evidence are public.

The official summaries and fixed estimator settings derive from Zelzy's Apache-2.0 OBSCURA starter. Spectral descriptors are independently implemented from mathematical ideas in the cited literature; no third-party fire implementation is vendored. OpenAI Codex assisted implementation, tests, research, analysis automation, interface work and writing. Original observations are unchanged; no generated labels or invented results are used. Source is released under Apache-2.0 with upstream attribution.
